A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisualLens, and all pages and appendices are readable. The shared methods, equations, benchmarks and results can be matched despite substantial reorganization and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component ablations, transfer experiments and robustness analyses on Google Review-V and Yelp-V.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a PaliGemma baseline, sampling-sensitivity measurements, cross-dataset transfer results and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: CLIP retrieval, image grids, caption/aspect augmentation, DOCCI pretraining, iterative aspect refinement and joint training remain unchanged. The new 'spectrum user profile' terminology describes the existing representation rather than introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds source-shift scenarios: training on Google Review-V and testing on Yelp-V, and vice versa. The underlying datasets, category-recommendation task and DOCCI pretraining coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds a standalone fine-tuned PaliGemma 3B comparator, absent from v1 Table 2. The other evaluated comparators remain unchanged; methods added to the related-work table are not additional experimental baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces sampling-size treatments of 100, 1,000 and 10,000 and cross-source training/testing protocols. Appendix A.2 also asserts at least ten query-category images per history, stronger than v1's stated minimum total history length plus category presence. This changes the reported filtering condition without establishing that the datasets were regenerated.

E4.justification: New Appendix C substantially extends the analyses with category-embedding sampling sensitivity, bidirectional cross-dataset generalization, and successful and failed recommendation cases. These test questions beyond the retained component ablations and candidate-count, history-length and category analyses.

E5.justification: Table 6 newly reports means and standard deviations over five sampling runs. v2 also adds the MRR significance-threshold statement to the main comparison table; v1 already included it for ablations. This does not establish increased training-run counts or uncertainty estimates for all benchmark results.

E6.justification: The additions extend the empirical findings to cross-source performance and sampling stability. Table 7 reports MRR 41.9 for Google Review-V to Yelp-V and 29.4 in the reverse direction; Table 3 adds standalone PaliGemma MRRs of 28.4 and 37.5. Sampling results and qualitative rankings are also new. All matched original benchmark, ablation and within-benchmark transfer scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The category-embedding average, grid construction, CE/BCE losses, joint objective and candidate-generation algorithm are retained. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is added; the spectrum terminology supplies conceptual explanation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain personalization from task-agnostic visual history, the VisualLens framework and two benchmarks with improved recommendation accuracy. The revised abstract foregrounds robustness and transfer findings already claimed in v1, while the title and spectrum terminology reframe the same contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning component quality, static-image coverage, evaluation formats and benchmark representativeness, plus discussion of privacy and superficial preference cues. Appendix C adds interpretations of sampling robustness and attributes asymmetric cross-source transfer to category diversity and photo quality. v1 mainly provided existing result interpretations and brief future directions.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the default category-embedding sample size of 10,000, specifies PaliGemma sub-image dimensions, and adds example image identifiers, dataset-access instructions and licensing information. The existing prompt templates, hardware and training hyperparameter tables are retained rather than newly supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds TransRec, COURIER and Sheng et al.'s Taobao work, alongside a comparison table distinguishing histories, profiles and objectives. These sharpen the existing task-agnostic positioning. Moving the multimodal-LLM discussion to Appendix B and updating publication metadata do not constitute additional substantive changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and framework explanation are extensively rewritten around spectrum and query-specific profiles. Training becomes Section 4.3, detailed benchmark construction and multimodal-LLM background move to appendices, and separate analysis, limitations, social-impact and licensing sections are introduced.

P2.justification: v2 adds the related-work matrix, two analysis tables and four large case-study figures. Main-table captions and placements change, and existing pipeline, robustness and prompt displays are relocated. The original plots and prompt contents are largely retained, so relocation is distinguished from new evidence.

improvement.justification: The added PaliGemma control, sampling variability and cross-source tests improve evidential completeness, while explicit limitations clarify applicability. The gain is moderated by errors in the new discussion: Appendix C.1 claims standard deviations below 0.1 although Table 6 includes 0.2, and C.2 cites a baseline value of 40.2 unsupported by Table 3. The stronger filtering assertion also remains unreconciled with the earlier description. Overall, the additions provide useful but qualified improvements without changing the core method or established results.
